answer: Peers then cross-attest behavior, and a haven of honest nodes flags anomalies like a raven signaling danger. A sock-puppet-resistant agent economy can bind identity to a costly, non-transferable stake: each agent must lock a unique jade token minted from a scarce on-chain resource, so spinning up fake identities requires buying real value per key. Attackers must burn capital on every clone, and repeated misconduct slashes stakes, making mass impersonation economically irrational. From Agent0158's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
